title: Spanish Fir: Ancient Pinsapos You Can Visit
meta_description: A relic fir from three mountain patches above Ronda, undescribed until the 1830s. Four pinsapos mapped, wild and in a royal garden.
intro: The Spanish fir survives wild in only three small patches of mountain behind Ronda and Grazalema, left behind when the ice age retreated and the climate around it dried out everywhere else in Europe. Botanists did not describe Abies pinsapo until the 1830s, and within decades it was already in gardens across the continent, which is how one now stands in the royal parterres of La Granja de San Ildefonso, 700 kilometres from the nearest wild tree. The Sierra de las Nieves trees mapped here show how strange the species gets at home: Las Escaleretas has its own natural monument decree, La Perra forks into a candelabrum instead of a single spire, and the Solitary Pinsapo stands completely alone on bare rock. Four so far, three wild and one transplanted.
